To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
T cell growth factor is essential for the growth of a T chronic lymphocytic leukemia.
T cell growth factor can restore mitogen and allostimulation in a T cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia patient with defective T cell responsiveness.
T-cell growth factor-mediated T-CLL cell proliferation is a consequence of the failure of these leukemic T cells to produce T-cell growth factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the functional and biochemical abnormalities of a T-CLL cell line, T-CLL 2, which was established from peripheral blood lymphocytes of a patient suffering from T-CLL.
the study of T-CLL cells which have lost their responsiveness to T cell mitogens and allo-antigens, but which can be induced to proliferate and differentiate by TCGF.
the study of the proliferative response of T cells from a patient with T-CLL to various stimuli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T-CLLeukaemic cell line has been shown to be defective in the production of TCGF and in its response to mitogens.
the T-CLT PBL were unable to respond to TCGF and alloantigents, and that this was due to a lack of production of TCGF by these cells.
the T-CLl PBL were defective in TCGF production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T-CLL is a disease of T-lymphocytes with a defect in T cell growth factor production.
the T-CLLLPBL are defective in their ability to produce TCGFa.
T-CLL cells have a defect in the production of TCGF, which is not due to an intrinsic defect in the T-CLP cells but is caused by the presence of suppressor cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TCGF is not only a mitogen for T lymphocytes, but is also an essential factor in the induction of T cell responses.
the lack of T cell responsiveness of T-CLL cells is not due to the absence of Ia-like molecules on the cell surface but to the lack of production of TCGF.
the T cell growth factor-mediated proliferation is an effective way to stimulate the proliferation of T-CLL lymphocytes.
